story_type: airliner braking tests on runways flooded on purpose, historic film
hook: They flooded the runway on purpose. Then landed a jet.
narration: This jet was trying to stop on a runway that had been flooded on purpose.
NASA's Langley experts wanted to know how long a jet takes to stop on a wet runway.
A layer of water can get between a tire and the pavement, so the brakes grip less and the stop gets longer.
With the Air Force and the FAA, they flooded runways at several airports, time after time.
Then ground vehicles and the test aircraft tried stopping on the wet pavement.
outcome: The tests gave engineers new knowledge of runway friction, aimed at safer stops for aircraft in bad weather.
title: Jet stops on a flooded runway
question_comment: Have you ever felt a plane brake hard on a wet runway?
